title: Evaluated pure reduction multiplication triangle
statement: Let ell be prime, W any scheme, D a diagonal derived reduction and eta its quotient-normalized evaluated units [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface, lem-sfb-diagonal-evaluation-unit]. Let M be any integral pro-etale sheaf and b:T(M[1])≅H[2] a supplied pure-system comparison. There are arrows d_n:U(H_n)→M such that (ell^(n+1), eta_n followed by the canonical evaluated comparison of b, single(d_n)[2] followed by shift addition) is a distinguished triangle on single(M)[1], and U(H_(n+1)→H_n) followed by d_n equals d_(n+1) followed by ell. No roots, finite Tate lines or Kummer classes occur.

source.place: Steps (2) and (3), the common two-term resolution and its (ell,1) transition.

proof.text: Use diagonal_reduction_resolution to choose one common representative P of M[1] on which all positive prime powers are degreewise monic and the supplied D counit is invertible. The ordinary quotient comparison gives diagonal_evaluation_complex_shortExact for the actual evaluated quotient-unit map at every level.

Compose the inverse counit, D applied to the resolution comparison, and the supplied b to obtain one pure-system comparison for the termwise reduction. Evaluate it using the exact-derived factorization comparisons. The normalized complexes equation for eta and its naturality identify every quotient arrow with the prescribed eta followed by the original b comparison. Localize the evaluation-transition transformation; its compatibility with exact single and shift comparisons proves that the evaluated purity comparisons respect quotient transitions.

Apply pure_multiplication_triangle_assembly to these compatible short exact sequences and pure comparisons. Its fully faithful shifted-single argument produces the ordinary d_n, its transported short-exact triangle has exactly the prescribed middle arrow, and its (ell,identity,quotient) naturality square gives the required ordinary boundary identity.
